text.p: European number one Colin Montgomerie rediscovered his putting touch and broke out of a slump by winning the European zone of the Andersen Consulting World Championship in decisive fashion on Tuesday.

A new putter he was sent only on Monday night sparked his confidence and brought him a 6 and 4 thrashing of fellow Scot Sam Torrence in the morning semi-final followed by a comprehensive defeat of Italy's Costantino Rocca by 5 and 4 in the final.

A stunning run of seven birdies in 10 holes from the second after he had lost the opening hole carried the world number six into the world final against the winners of the other three zones in Arizona next January.
Montgomerie collected $200,000 for his victory and he can boost his earnings from the event to $1 million if he emerges as the champion at Grayhawk.
Montgomerie's performance against Rocca was irrestible and ended when Rocca bogeyed the 14th hole at the Buckinghamshire course.
His semifinal also finished on the 14th and he was 14 under for his 28 holes and delighted with all aspects of his game.

"My putting's back but my iron play set up so many opportunities," said Montgomerie. "That was because I was coming off the middle of the fairway all the time. This augurs well not just for the final of this tournament but for the rest of the year."

In the morning Montgomerie had rekindled his touch with a 30-footer to square his match with Torrance on the fourth and when he followed up with a 15-foot eagle putt on the fifth, his compatriot, too, had no answer, conceding at the short 14th.
Rocca joined Montgomerie in the final by coming back from three down after only four holes to Northern Ireland's Darren Clarke, winning their match at the 19th with a birdie.

Having won this matchplay event, Montgomerie talked about the more important Ryder Cup in September, where he could be partnering Nick Faldo, although the Englishman may have to rely on a wild card from captain Severiano Ballesteros.
Faldo is in England for this week's Volvo PGA Championship and the captain wants the pair to play together.

In desperate straits over his putting even though he won his first round match here on Monday, Montgomerie put out an SOS phone call to his putter suppliers, whose factory is only a few miles from his home.
"I asked them to send round three putters. I chose one after a putting session on my carpet and left at 5.30 AM today to putt for an hour with it at the course before anybody arrived.
"I think my hard work's beginning to pay off. I've never worked so hard on one aspect of my game before," he said.

The other finalists will be Hajime Meshiai from the Japanese zone, Davis Love III from the American leg and the winner of the international zone in which defending overall champion Greg Norman of Australia plays on July 28-29 in Wisconsin.
